publications.title: The Catechol Benchmark: Time-series Solvent Selection Data for Few-shot Machine Learning
publications.authors: T Boyne, JS Campos, BD Langdon, J Qing, Y Xie, S Zhang, C Tsay, ...
publications.tldr: The Catechol Benchmark introduces the first transient flow dataset for few-shot machine learning in chemistry, with over 1200 data points for allyl substituted catechol rearrangement. Utilizing continuous solvent mixtures, temperature, and residence time ramps, this dataset provides dense, time-series yield data. It enables benchmarking of regression, transfer learning, and active learning algorithms for complex solvent selection tasks, posing new challenges for ML models due to continuous parameter variations. This dataset supports applications in sustainable manufacturing and solvent replacement.
publications.abstract: Machine learning has promised to change the landscape of laboratory chemistry, with impressive results in molecular property prediction and reaction retro-synthesis. However, chemical datasets are often inaccessible to the machine learning community as they tend to require cleaning, thorough understanding of the chemistry, or are simply not available. In this paper, we introduce a novel dataset for yield prediction, providing the first-ever transient flow dataset for machine learning benchmarking, covering over 1200 process conditions. While previous datasets focus on discrete parameters, our experimental set-up allow us to sample a large number of continuous process conditions, generating new challenges for machine learning models. We focus on solvent selection, a task that is particularly difficult to model theoretically and therefore ripe for machine learning applications. We showcase benchmarking for regression algorithms, transfer-learning approaches, feature engineering, and active learning, with important applications towards solvent replacement and sustainable manufacturing.

publications.title: Global optimization of graph acquisition functions for neural architecture search
publications.authors: Y Xie, S Zhang, J Qing, R Misener, C Tsay
publications.tldr: This paper introduces NAS-GOAT for globally optimizing graph acquisition functions in Neural Architecture Search (NAS) using Graph Bayesian Optimization. It proposes a novel, equivalent variable-space encoding for general labeled graphs, including reachability and shortest paths, applicable to weakly connected acyclic NAS architectures. By formulating the acquisition function (e.g., LCB with shortest-path kernels) as a Mixed-Integer Program, NAS-GOAT offers theoretical optimality guarantees. Experimental results on NAS benchmarks demonstrate its efficiency in finding optimal neural architectures.
publications.abstract: Graph Bayesian optimization (BO) has shown potential as a powerful and data-efficient tool for neural architecture search (NAS). Most existing graph BO works focus on developing graph surrogates models, i.e., metrics of networks and/or different kernels to quantify the similarity between networks. However, the acquisition optimization, as a discrete optimization task over graph structures, is not well studied due to the complexity of formulating the graph search space and acquisition functions. This paper presents explicit optimization formulations for graph input space including properties such as reachability and shortest paths, which are used later to formulate graph kernels and the acquisition function. We theoretically prove that the proposed encoding is an equivalent representation of the graph space and provide restrictions for the NAS domain with either node or edge labels. Numerical results over several NAS benchmarks show that our method efficiently finds the optimal architecture for most cases, highlighting its efficacy.

publications.title: System-Aware Neural ODE Processes for Few-Shot Bayesian Optimization
publications.authors: Jixiang Qing, Becky D Langdon, Robert M Lee, Behrang Shafei, Mark van der ...
publications.tldr: This paper introduces System-Aware Neural ODE Processes (SANODEP) for few-shot Bayesian Optimization (BO) in dynamical systems with unknown, expensive-to-evaluate ODEs. SANODEP extends Neural ODE Processes (NODEP) by meta-learning ODE *systems* from multiple trajectories via a novel context embedding block, enabling rapid adaptation with minimal data. A two-stage BO framework optimizes initial conditions and termination times under measurement delay constraints. Experiments demonstrate SANODEP's superior performance over standard BO models, highlighting the benefits of its ODE-aware, meta-learning architecture.
publications.abstract: We consider the problem of optimizing initial conditions and termination time in dynamical systems governed by unknown ordinary differential equations (ODEs), where evaluating different initial conditions is costly and the state's value can not be measured in real-time but only with a delay while the measuring device processes the sample. To identify the optimal conditions in limited trials, we introduce a few-shot Bayesian Optimization (BO) framework based on the system's prior information. At the core of our approach is the System-Aware Neural ODE Processes (SANODEP), an extension of Neural ODE Processes (NODEP) designed to meta-learn ODE systems from multiple trajectories using a novel context embedding block. We further develop a two-stage BO framework to effectively incorporate search space constraints, enabling efficient optimization of both initial conditions and observation timings. We conduct extensive experiments showcasing SANODEP's potential for few-shot BO within dynamical systems. We also explore SANODEP's adaptability to varying levels of prior information, highlighting the trade-off between prior flexibility and model fitting accuracy.

publications.title: BoGrape: Bayesian optimization over graphs with shortest-path encoded
publications.authors: Y Xie, S Zhang, J Qing, R Misener, C Tsay
publications.tldr: BoGrape presents a Bayesian optimization framework for optimizing expensive black-box functions over *attributed graph structures*. It leverages Gaussian Processes as surrogates, employing novel shortest-path (SP, SSP) and exponential shortest-path (ESP, ESSP) graph kernels. Crucially, BoGrape formulates the acquisition function optimization as a Mixed-Integer Optimization Problem (MIP) by encoding shortest paths. This enables global, feasible exploration of the graph search space, guaranteeing optimal acquisition solutions, which is demonstrated effectively in molecular design.
publications.abstract: Graph-structured data play an important role across science and industry. This paper asks: how can we optimize over graphs, for instance to find the best graph structure and/or node features that minimize an expensive-to-evaluate black-box objective? Such problem settings arise, e.g., in molecular design, neural architecture search, and sensor placement. Bayesian optimization is a powerful tool for optimizing black-box functions, and existing technologies can be applied to optimize functions over nodes of a single fixed graph. We present Bayesian optimization acquisition functions for a class of shortest-path kernels and formulate them as mixed-integer optimization problems, enabling global exploration of the graph domain while maintaining solution feasibility when problem-specific constraints are present. We demonstrate our proposed approach, BoGrape, on several molecular design case studies.

publications.title: Molecular design using graph Bayesian optimization with shortest-path kernels
publications.authors: Y Xie, S Zhang, J Qing, R Misener, C Tsay
publications.venue: ICLR 2025 Workshop on Generative and Experimental Perspectives for …, 2025
publications.tldr: BoGrape introduces a graph Bayesian optimization framework for molecular design, leveraging Gaussian Processes with four novel shortest-path graph kernels (SP, SSP, ESP, ESSP) for molecular similarity. Its core contribution is optimizing acquisition functions via a Mixed-Integer Program (MIP), precisely encoding shortest paths as decision variables. This approach enables global exploration and ensures molecular validity within discrete search spaces. Preliminary results on QM7/QM9 datasets demonstrate promising performance and sample efficiency for optimal molecular design.
publications.abstract: Past decades have seen the great potential of generative machine learning in molecular design while also exposed the gap between research contributions and practical applications. Considering the expensive-to-evaluate nature of molecular properties and hard-to-satisfy validity of molecular structures, this paper tackles molecular design from graph Bayesian optimization viewpoint, i.e., generating feasible and optimal molecular graph with compatible features given limited number of evaluations. Our proposed method, BoGrape, uses shortest-path graph kernels to measure the similarity between molecules and utilizes mixed-integer programming to allow global exploration of molecular space while maintaining the feasibility of generated candidates. Preliminary results show promising performance of BoGrape.

publications.title: Knee detection in bayesian multi-objective optimization using thompson sampling
publications.authors: A Heidari, J Qing, SR Gonzalez, J Branke, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
publications.tldr: This paper proposes a novel Bayesian Optimization framework utilizing Thompson Sampling to efficiently detect "knee regions" in multi-objective optimization. By focusing on these preferred trade-off areas rather than the entire Pareto front, the method offers a computationally efficient alternative. Experimental results demonstrate its accuracy in locating single and multiple knee regions with very few function evaluations, significantly reducing the computational cost of identifying attractive solutions for decision-makers.
publications.abstract: Real-world problems often consist of multiple conflicting objectives to be optimized simultaneously, featuring a set of Pareto-optimal solutions. Estimating the entire Pareto front can be computationally expensive, and is not always necessary, as decision makers will likely be interested only in specific regions of the Pareto front. In the absence of knowledge about the decision maker preferences, the so-called knees in the Pareto front are considered to be particularly attractive. In this paper, we propose using Thompson Sampling in the Bayesian optimization framework to estimate the location of the knee regions in a data-efficient manner. Our experimental results show that the proposed methods accurately locate the knee regions after a very small number of evaluations, providing a computationally efficient approach to single-and multi-knee detection in multi-objective optimization.

publications.title: Wind turbine hybrid physics-based deep learning model for a health monitoring approach considering provision of ancillary services
publications.authors: N Kayedpour, J Qing, J Wauters, JDM De Kooning, I Couckuyt, ...
publications.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement 73, 1-14, 2024
publications.tldr: A novel hybrid physics-based deep learning framework is introduced for wind turbine (WT) health monitoring, particularly under ancillary service and curtailment operations. This framework accurately models WT aerodynamic nonlinearity. It incorporates a computationally efficient weakly supervised method for degradation and anomaly detection, complemented by a self-learning classifier that dynamically adapts to unforeseen abnormalities. The approach significantly improves health monitoring performance by effectively handling system uncertainties, like wind stochasticity and data sparsity, leading to more efficient and accurate WT condition assessment.
publications.abstract: Assessing the overall condition of wind turbines (WTs) in operation is challenging due to their intricate nature. This becomes even more complicated when WTs provide ancillary services and respond to grid requirements under curtailment modes. Multiple models are required to effectively evaluate the WTs’ healthy condition, which can be unmanageable and impractical, particularly for large-scale wind farms. This article proposes a novel hybrid physics-based deep learning framework to accurately approximate the time-varying correlation between control sequences and system response, reflecting the aerodynamic nonlinearity of the 5-MW offshore WT model, designed and tested by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL). Another layer of this study’s novelty relies on proposing a computationally efficient weakly supervised method that uses the hybrid structure to detect degradations and anomalies considering curtailment operation. Then, a self-learning classification approach is employed to iteratively update the best-tuned classifier, dynamically learning unforeseen abnormalities from brand-new anomalies during active operations. The proposed anomaly detection strategy deals with system uncertainties, such as wind stochasticity, power curve variations, and different sparsity levels in the datasets. The results of the proposed approach show promise in improving health monitoring performance, leading to a more efficient and accurate assessment of the overall condition of WTs.

publications.title: A robust multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework considering input uncertainty
publications.authors: J Qing, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene
publications.tldr: This paper presents a novel framework for multi-objective Bayesian optimization considering input uncertainty. It proposes a robust Gaussian Process model to infer the Bayes risk criterion, quantifying solution robustness. A two-stage Bayesian optimization process then searches for a robust Pareto frontier, identifying solutions with strong average performance despite input variations. The framework supports various uncertainty distributions, leverages parallel computing, and demonstrates effectiveness on numerical benchmarks.
publications.abstract: Bayesian optimization is a popular tool for optimizing time-consuming objective functions with a limited number of function evaluations. In real-life applications like engineering design, the designer often wants to take multiple objectives as well as input uncertainty into account to find a set of robust solutions. While this is an active topic in single-objective Bayesian optimization, it is less investigated in the multi-objective case. We introduce a novel Bayesian optimization framework to perform multi-objective optimization considering input uncertainty. We propose a robust Gaussian Process model to infer the Bayes risk criterion to quantify robustness, and we develop a two-stage Bayesian optimization process to search for a robust Pareto frontier, i.e., solutions that have good average performance under input uncertainty. The complete framework supports various distributions of the input uncertainty and takes full advantage of parallel computing. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework through numerical benchmarks.

publications.title: {PF}ES: Parallel Feasible Pareto Frontier Entropy Search for Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
publications.authors: J Qing, HB Moss, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
publications.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics, 2565-2588, 2023
publications.tldr: {PF}2ES introduces a novel information-theoretic acquisition function for multi-objective Bayesian optimization, supporting unknown constraints and batch queries. It addresses the challenge of efficiently and accurately estimating mutual information between candidate evaluations and the feasible Pareto frontier. By utilizing a variational lower bound, {PF}2ES provides a low-cost, accurate estimate, overcoming the limitations of crude approximations or expensive inference in prior methods. Benchmarking demonstrates {PF}2ES achieves competitive optimization performance across synthetic and real-world design problems.
publications.abstract: We present Parallel Feasible Pareto Frontier Entropy Search ({PF}2ES) — a novel information-theoretic acquisition function for multi-objective Bayesian optimization supporting unknown constraints and batch queries. Due to the complexity of characterizing the mutual information between candidate evaluations and (feasible) Pareto frontiers, existing approaches must either employ crude approximations that significantly hamper their performance or rely on expensive inference schemes that substantially increase the optimization's computational overhead. By instead using a variational lower bound, {PF}2ES provides a low-cost and accurate estimate of the mutual information. We benchmark {PF}2ES against other information-theoretic acquisition functions, demonstrating its competitive performance for optimization across synthetic and real-world design problems.

publications.title: Trieste: Efficiently exploring the depths of black-box functions with tensorflow
publications.authors: V Picheny, J Berkeley, HB Moss, H Stojic, U Granta, SW Ober, A Artemev, ...
publications.tldr: Trieste is an open-source Python package for scalable Bayesian Optimization (BO) and active learning, leveraging TensorFlow 2.x. It provides a modular framework for plug-and-play integration of TensorFlow-based probabilistic models (e.g., GPflow, Keras NNs) and custom acquisition functions. Trieste efficiently addresses BO's sequential nature by preventing expensive computational graph retracing. Key features include flexible `AskTellOptimizer`/`BayesianOptimizer` interfaces, diverse model support, and optimized acquisition functions utilizing automatic differentiation, enabling robust and extensible black-box function exploration.
publications.abstract: We present Trieste, an open-source Python package for Bayesian optimization and active learning benefiting from the scalability and efficiency of TensorFlow. Our library enables the plug-and-play of popular TensorFlow-based models within sequential decision-making loops, e.g. Gaussian processes from GPflow or GPflux, or neural networks from Keras. This modular mindset is central to the package and extends to our acquisition functions and the internal dynamics of the decision-making loop, both of which can be tailored and extended by researchers or engineers when tackling custom use cases. Trieste is a research-friendly and production-ready toolkit backed by a comprehensive test suite, extensive documentation, and available at https://github.com/secondmind-labs/trieste.

publications.title: Bayesian active learning for engineering design and optimization under uncertainty
publications.authors: J Qing

publications.title: Finding knees in bayesian multi-objective optimization
publications.authors: A Heidari, J Qing, S Rojas Gonzalez, J Branke, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
publications.venue: International Conference on Parallel Problem Solving from Nature, 104-117, 2022
publications.tldr: This paper introduces novel acquisition functions within Bayesian Multi-Objective Optimization to efficiently identify "knee" solutions on the Pareto front. Knees represent desirable trade-off points, and this work addresses their detection based on two specific definitions. The proposed acquisition functions enable data-efficient discovery of these solutions, minimizing costly evaluations. This approach effectively scales to problems with many objectives, demonstrating promising results on various benchmarks.
publications.abstract: Multi-objective optimization requires many evaluations to identify a sufficiently dense approximation of the Pareto front. Especially for a higher number of objectives, extracting the Pareto front might not be easy nor cheap. On the other hand, the Decision-Maker is not always interested in the entire Pareto front, and might prefer a solution where there is a desirable trade-off between different objectives. An example of an attractive solution is the knee point of the Pareto front, although the current literature differs on the definition of a knee. In this work, we propose to detect knee solutions in a data-efficient manner (i.e., with a limited number of time-consuming evaluations), according to two definitions of knees. In particular, we propose several novel acquisition functions in the Bayesian Optimization framework for detecting these knees, which allows for scaling to many objectives. The suggested acquisition functions are evaluated on various benchmarks with promising results.

publications.title: Adaptive sampling with automatic stopping for feasible region identification in engineering design
publications.authors: J Qing, N Knudde, F Garbuglia, D Spina, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene
publications.tldr: This paper presents an adaptive sampling methodology for identifying feasible regions in engineering design. It utilizes Gaussian process metamodels to estimate multi-constraint feasible regions, employing an information-based adaptive sampling strategy for sequential refinement. A novel framework is introduced to automatically stop the sampling process by estimating the metamodel's prediction accuracy. The proposed approach demonstrates improved efficiency, accuracy, and robustness compared to state-of-the-art techniques.
publications.abstract: Engineering design is a complex process to find a suitable trade-off among different, and sometimes conflicting, design specifications. In reality, these requirements can be often considered as constraints of the design problem, that can be defined in terms of performance measures or geometrical characteristics of the device under study. In this paper, a new design space exploration methodology is presented for discovering feasible regions in the design space, where the term feasible region indicates the set of all design configurations satisfying all constraints of the design problem. The proposed method is based on Gaussian process metamodels to estimate the feasible region and leverages a information-based adaptive sampling technique to sequentially refine the prediction accuracy, which is applicable for multiple constraints problems. To efficiently stop the adaptive sampling process, a novel framework to estimate the metamodel’s prediction accuracy is proposed. The efficiency, accuracy and robustness of the proposed approach are compared with state-of-art techniques on suitable benchmark problems and practical engineering examples.

publications.title: A robust bayesian optimization framework for microwave circuit design under uncertainty
publications.authors: D De Witte, J Qing, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene, D Vande Ginste, D Spina
publications.tldr: This paper presents a novel, data-efficient Bayesian Optimization framework for robust microwave circuit design under inevitable parameter uncertainties. It achieves robustness by modifying the Expected Improvement (EI) criterion to explicitly account for design parameter variations like manufacturing tolerances. This approach efficiently identifies designs insensitive to uncertainties early in the design cycle, significantly improving robustness with fewer simulations compared to standard methods, as validated by application examples.
publications.abstract: In modern electronics, there are many inevitable uncertainties and variations of design parameters that have a profound effect on the performance of a device. These are, among others, induced by manufacturing tolerances, assembling inaccuracies, material diversities, machining errors, etc. This prompts wide interests in enhanced optimization algorithms that take the effect of these uncertainty sources into account and that are able to find robust designs, i.e., designs that are insensitive to the uncertainties early in the design cycle. In this work, a novel machine learning-based optimization framework that accounts for uncertainty of the design parameters is presented. This is achieved by using a modified version of the expected improvement criterion. Moreover, a data-efficient Bayesian Optimization framework is leveraged to limit the number of simulations required to find a robust design solution. Two suitable application examples validate that the robustness is significantly improved compared to standard design methods.

publications.title: Spectral representation of robustness measures for optimization under input uncertainty
publications.authors: J Qing, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
publications.tldr: This paper introduces a Spectral Representation of Robustness Measures (SRRM) to analytically infer mean-variance robustness under Gaussian Process (GP) models. Addressing the challenge of Bayesian variance inference, SRRM leverages GP's spectral representation to approximate robustness for normal and uniform input uncertainties. Two Fourier feature-based approximations are proposed and compared. Integrated into robust Bayesian Optimization acquisition functions, SRRM demonstrates competitive performance on numerical benchmarks and real-world applications.
publications.abstract: We study the inference of mean-variance robustness measures to quantify input uncertainty under the Gaussian Process (GP) framework. These measures are widely used in applications where the robustness of the solution is of interest, for example, in engineering design. While the variance is commonly used to characterize the robustness, Bayesian inference of the variance using GPs is known to be challenging. In this paper, we propose a Spectral Representation of Robustness Measures based on the GP’s spectral representation, i.e., an analytical approach to approximately infer both robustness measures for normal and uniform input uncertainty distributions. We present two approximations based on different Fourier features and compare their accuracy numerically. To demonstrate their utility and efficacy in robust Bayesian Optimization, we integrate the analytical robustness measures in three standard acquisition functions for various robust optimization formulations. We show their competitive performance on numerical benchmarks and real-life applications.

publications.title: Hovering efficiency optimization of the ducted propeller with weight penalty taken into account
publications.authors: Y Hu, J xiang Qing, ZH Liu, ZJ Conrad, JN Cao, XP Zhang
publications.tldr: This paper optimizes ducted propeller hovering efficiency, incorporating structural weight penalty. It reveals weight penalty dominates at low disk loading, while aerodynamic efficiency is key at high disk loading. Multi-objective optimization shows ducted propellers can surpass open propellers in overall efficiency, even at low disk loading. Optimal designs feature a large inner lip radius, small outer lip radius, and a short/no diffuser. This emphasizes the inner lip's primary aerodynamic contribution, achieving significant weight reduction with limited efficiency loss for compact, easily integrated systems.
publications.abstract: The ducted propeller is superior to the open propeller in hovering efficiency. However, the overall system efficiency of a ducted propeller is reduced due to its heavy structure. If the weight penalty is taken into account, will the ducted propeller still be superior to an open propeller? And in this scenario, how will a ducted propeller with better efficiency than an open propeller be designed? This paper investigates these questions by parametric analysis based on experiments and then parametric optimization that involves hovering efficiency and structural weight in objective functions. Both multi-disciplinary design optimization and multi-objective programming are performed by surrogate-based optimization. An in-house automatic structured mesh generation module is developed to deal with significant geometry variation in design space. Finally, the optimization results are validated by post-optimization experiments. The results of experiment and optimization indicate that the effects of weight penalty play a leading role at low disk loading and hence in this case, the one with lighter structure is superior. But at high disk loading, as thrust gets higher, the leading factor turns into aerodynamic hovering efficiency, therefore the one with higher aerodynamic hovering efficiency prevails. The multi-objective optimization produces an L-shaped Pareto front, and the optimum of multi-disciplinary optimization is quite close to the Pareto front knee point. The designs in this region encounter limited aerodynamic hovering efficiency loss but gain significant weight reduction. Therefore, we can obtain a ducted propeller superior to an open propeller in system efficiency with pretty low disk loading, although the weight penalty is considered. These designs feature a relatively large inner lip radius, a small outer lip radius, and a short or even no diffuser. This means that the inner lip radius contributes the most to the aerodynamic hovering efficiency, followed by the diffuser and outer lip. These designs have very low height to diameter ratio therefore they can be easily integrated into aircraft structure.

publications.title: Bayesian active learning for multi‐objective feasible region identification in microwave devices
publications.authors: F Garbuglia, J Qing, N Knudde, D Spina, I Couckuyt, D Deschrijver, ...
publications.tldr: This paper presents a novel Bayesian active learning framework for multi-objective feasible region identification in microwave device design. It leverages a stochastic model to efficiently and accurately pinpoint designs satisfying multiple specifications, significantly reducing the number of simulations required. The proposed automated procedure rapidly obtains suitable designs, validated through an application example, offering a more resource-efficient design optimization approach.
publications.abstract: In microwave device and circuit design, many simulations are often needed to find a set of designs that satisfy one or multiple specifications chosen by the designer upfront: the feasible region. A novel Bayesian active learning framework is presented to accurately identify the feasible region with a low number of simulations. The technique leverages on a stochastic model to obtain an efficient and automated procedure. A suitable application example validates the proposed technique and shows its effectiveness to rapidly obtain many suitable designs.

publications.title: Batch Bayesian active learning for feasible region identification by local penalization
publications.authors: J Qing, N Knudde, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene, K Shintani
publications.tldr: This paper proposes a batch Bayesian active learning technique for efficiently identifying feasible regions in engineering design, overcoming the high cost of constraint evaluations. Unlike sequential methods, it selects multiple samples per iteration, leveraging computational resources. The method assumes Lipschitz continuous constraint functions and extends existing batch active learning techniques to this specific task. Experiments demonstrate its superior performance in feasible region identification compared to these extended state-of-the-art batch methods.
publications.abstract: Identifying all designs satisfying a set of constraints is an important part of the engineering design process. With physics-based simulation codes, evaluating the constraints becomes considerable expensive. Active learning can provide an elegant approach to efficiently characterize the feasible region, i.e., the set of feasible designs. Although active learning strategies have been proposed for this task, most of them are dealing with adding just one sample per iteration as opposed to selecting multiple samples per iteration, also known as batch active learning. While this is efficient with respect to the amount of information gained per iteration, it neglects available computation resources. We propose a batch Bayesian active learning technique for feasible region identification by assuming that the constraint function is Lipschitz continuous. In addition, we extend current state-of-the-art batch methods to also handle feasible region identification. Experiments show better performance of the proposed method than the extended batch methods.

publications.title: Bayesian active learning for electromagnetic structure design
publications.authors: J Qing, N Knudde, I Couckuyt, D Spina, T Dhaene
publications.venue: 2020 14th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP), 1-5, 2020
publications.tldr: This paper presents a novel Bayesian active learning framework for electromagnetic structure design. It utilizes an entropy search-based strategy, powered by a Gaussian Process model, to efficiently identify design configurations that meet specific requirements. The core contribution is minimizing the number of time-consuming computer simulations or expensive design trials needed, thereby accelerating the design process. An application example validates its effectiveness.
publications.abstract: A novel design framework based on Bayesian active learning is presented in this contribution. The proposed approach allows one to identify a set of design configurations satisfying the chosen specification. In particular, the entropy search-based active learning strategy, which relies on a Gaussian Process model, is able to minimize the number of time-consuming computer simulations or expensive design trials necessary to reach this goal. A suitable application example validates the proposed method.

publications.title: Kriging Assisted Integrated Rotor-Duct Optimization for Ducted Fan in Hover
publications.authors: J Qing, Y Hu, Y Wang, Z Liu, X Fu, W Liu
publications.tldr: This paper presents a Kriging-assisted integrated rotor-duct optimization for ducted fans in hover, addressing limitations of separate optimizations. Using RANS with FFD/Bezier parameterizations, the objective was to maximize hovering efficiency under thrust constraints. Key finding: Integrated optimization achieves superior efficiency. It yields blades with longer tip chords, which injects more momentum into the duct's boundary layer, suppressing flow separation. This enables a larger diffuser expansion angle, resulting in a better overall hovering efficiency compared to un-integrated designs.
publications.abstract: The design of ducted fan was primarily based on parametric analysis and the existing optimization design studies mainly focus on either the rotor or the duct alone. However, the interactions between the rotor and duct remarkably affects the performance of the ducted fan. Therefore, it has been expected that an integrated optimization such the rotor-duct interactions are involved could result in a better design. In this paper, the integrated rotor-duct optimization was performed. Then it was compared with several different optimized configurations. The Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes solver incorporated with momentum source method was adopted to predict performance of ducted fan and it was validated by force measurement experiments. The duct shape was parameterized by the FFD method and the blade shape was modeled by Bezier splines. A surrogate based optimization framework using Kriging model was developed. The hovering efficiency was set as the objective function subjecting to the thrust constraint. The optima from different optimized configurations were analyzed with the help of crossover studies. The analysis revealed that the improvement of the ducted fan hovering efficiency is primarily restricted by the flow separations in the duct. When the shape of both the rotor and duct was involved into the design optimization, the blade with longer chord at blade tip was obtained. This helps injecting more momentum into the boundary layer of the duct and the flow separation can be suppressed. Therefore, the integrated rotor-duct optimization produces the duct with larger diffuser expansion angle and better hovering efficiency.

2025.authors: Jixiang Qing, Becky D Langdon, Robert M Lee, Behrang Shafei, Mark van der ...

A two-stage BO framework optimizes initial conditions and termination times under measurement delay constraints. Experiments demonstrate SANODEP's superior performance over standard BO models, highlighting the benefits of its ODE-aware, meta-learning architecture.
2025.abstract: We consider the problem of optimizing initial conditions and termination time in dynamical systems governed by unknown ordinary differential equations (ODEs), where evaluating different initial conditions is costly and the state's value can not be measured in real-time but only with a delay while the measuring device processes the sample. To identify the optimal conditions in limited trials, we introduce a few-shot Bayesian Optimization (BO) framework based on the system's prior information. At the core of our approach is the System-Aware Neural ODE Processes (SANODEP), an extension of Neural ODE Processes (NODEP) designed to meta-learn ODE systems from multiple trajectories using a novel context embedding block. We further develop a two-stage BO framework to effectively incorporate search space constraints, enabling efficient optimization of both initial conditions and observation timings. We conduct extensive experiments showcasing SANODEP's potential for few-shot BO within dynamical systems. We also explore SANODEP's adaptability to varying levels of prior information, highlighting the trade-off between prior flexibility and model fitting accuracy.

2025.title: BoGrape: Bayesian optimization over graphs with shortest-path encoded
2025.authors: Y Xie, S Zhang, J Qing, R Misener, C Tsay
2025.tldr: BoGrape presents a Bayesian optimization framework for optimizing expensive black-box functions over *attributed graph structures*. It leverages Gaussian Processes as surrogates, employing novel shortest-path (SP, SSP) and exponential shortest-path (ESP, ESSP) graph kernels. Crucially, BoGrape formulates the acquisition function optimization as a Mixed-Integer Optimization Problem (MIP) by encoding shortest paths. This enables global, feasible exploration of the graph search space, guaranteeing optimal acquisition solutions, which is demonstrated effectively in molecular design.
2025.abstract: Graph-structured data play an important role across science and industry. This paper asks: how can we optimize over graphs, for instance to find the best graph structure and/or node features that minimize an expensive-to-evaluate black-box objective? Such problem settings arise, e.g., in molecular design, neural architecture search, and sensor placement. Bayesian optimization is a powerful tool for optimizing black-box functions, and existing technologies can be applied to optimize functions over nodes of a single fixed graph. We present Bayesian optimization acquisition functions for a class of shortest-path kernels and formulate them as mixed-integer optimization problems, enabling global exploration of the graph domain while maintaining solution feasibility when problem-specific constraints are present. We demonstrate our proposed approach, BoGrape, on several molecular design case studies.

2025.title: Molecular design using graph Bayesian optimization with shortest-path kernels
2025.authors: Y Xie, S Zhang, J Qing, R Misener, C Tsay
2025.venue: ICLR 2025 Workshop on Generative and Experimental Perspectives for …, 2025
2025.tldr: BoGrape introduces a graph Bayesian optimization framework for molecular design, leveraging Gaussian Processes with four novel shortest-path graph kernels (SP, SSP, ESP, ESSP) for molecular similarity. Its core contribution is optimizing acquisition functions via a Mixed-Integer Program (MIP), precisely encoding shortest paths as decision variables. This approach enables global exploration and ensures molecular validity within discrete search spaces. Preliminary results on QM7/QM9 datasets demonstrate promising performance and sample efficiency for optimal molecular design.
2025.abstract: Past decades have seen the great potential of generative machine learning in molecular design while also exposed the gap between research contributions and practical applications. Considering the expensive-to-evaluate nature of molecular properties and hard-to-satisfy validity of molecular structures, this paper tackles molecular design from graph Bayesian optimization viewpoint, i.e., generating feasible and optimal molecular graph with compatible features given limited number of evaluations. Our proposed method, BoGrape, uses shortest-path graph kernels to measure the similarity between molecules and utilizes mixed-integer programming to allow global exploration of molecular space while maintaining the feasibility of generated candidates. Preliminary results show promising performance of BoGrape.

2025.title: A Meta-Learning Approach for Few-Shot Bayesian Optimization of Batch Chemical Processes
2025.authors: B Langdon, G Patron, J Qing, C Kappatou, RM Lee, B Shafei, R Misener, ...

2024.title: Knee detection in bayesian multi-objective optimization using thompson sampling
2024.authors: A Heidari, J Qing, SR Gonzalez, J Branke, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
2024.tldr: This paper proposes a novel Bayesian Optimization framework utilizing Thompson Sampling to efficiently detect "knee regions" in multi-objective optimization. By focusing on these preferred trade-off areas rather than the entire Pareto front, the method offers a computationally efficient alternative. Experimental results demonstrate its accuracy in locating single and multiple knee regions with very few function evaluations, significantly reducing the computational cost of identifying attractive solutions for decision-makers.
2024.abstract: Real-world problems often consist of multiple conflicting objectives to be optimized simultaneously, featuring a set of Pareto-optimal solutions. Estimating the entire Pareto front can be computationally expensive, and is not always necessary, as decision makers will likely be interested only in specific regions of the Pareto front. In the absence of knowledge about the decision maker preferences, the so-called knees in the Pareto front are considered to be particularly attractive. In this paper, we propose using Thompson Sampling in the Bayesian optimization framework to estimate the location of the knee regions in a data-efficient manner. Our experimental results show that the proposed methods accurately locate the knee regions after a very small number of evaluations, providing a computationally efficient approach to single-and multi-knee detection in multi-objective optimization.

2024.title: Wind turbine hybrid physics-based deep learning model for a health monitoring approach considering provision of ancillary services
2024.authors: N Kayedpour, J Qing, J Wauters, JDM De Kooning, I Couckuyt, ...
2024.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement 73, 1-14, 2024
2024.tldr: A novel hybrid physics-based deep learning framework is introduced for wind turbine (WT) health monitoring, particularly under ancillary service and curtailment operations. This framework accurately models WT aerodynamic nonlinearity. It incorporates a computationally efficient weakly supervised method for degradation and anomaly detection, complemented by a self-learning classifier that dynamically adapts to unforeseen abnormalities. The approach significantly improves health monitoring performance by effectively handling system uncertainties, like wind stochasticity and data sparsity, leading to more efficient and accurate WT condition assessment.
2024.abstract: Assessing the overall condition of wind turbines (WTs) in operation is challenging due to their intricate nature. This becomes even more complicated when WTs provide ancillary services and respond to grid requirements under curtailment modes. Multiple models are required to effectively evaluate the WTs’ healthy condition, which can be unmanageable and impractical, particularly for large-scale wind farms. This article proposes a novel hybrid physics-based deep learning framework to accurately approximate the time-varying correlation between control sequences and system response, reflecting the aerodynamic nonlinearity of the 5-MW offshore WT model, designed and tested by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL). Another layer of this study’s novelty relies on proposing a computationally efficient weakly supervised method that uses the hybrid structure to detect degradations and anomalies considering curtailment operation. Then, a self-learning classification approach is employed to iteratively update the best-tuned classifier, dynamically learning unforeseen abnormalities from brand-new anomalies during active operations. The proposed anomaly detection strategy deals with system uncertainties, such as wind stochasticity, power curve variations, and different sparsity levels in the datasets. The results of the proposed approach show promise in improving health monitoring performance, leading to a more efficient and accurate assessment of the overall condition of WTs.

2023.title: A robust multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework considering input uncertainty
2023.authors: J Qing, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene
2023.tldr: This paper presents a novel framework for multi-objective Bayesian optimization considering input uncertainty. It proposes a robust Gaussian Process model to infer the Bayes risk criterion, quantifying solution robustness. A two-stage Bayesian optimization process then searches for a robust Pareto frontier, identifying solutions with strong average performance despite input variations. The framework supports various uncertainty distributions, leverages parallel computing, and demonstrates effectiveness on numerical benchmarks.
2023.abstract: Bayesian optimization is a popular tool for optimizing time-consuming objective functions with a limited number of function evaluations. In real-life applications like engineering design, the designer often wants to take multiple objectives as well as input uncertainty into account to find a set of robust solutions. While this is an active topic in single-objective Bayesian optimization, it is less investigated in the multi-objective case. We introduce a novel Bayesian optimization framework to perform multi-objective optimization considering input uncertainty. We propose a robust Gaussian Process model to infer the Bayes risk criterion to quantify robustness, and we develop a two-stage Bayesian optimization process to search for a robust Pareto frontier, i.e., solutions that have good average performance under input uncertainty. The complete framework supports various distributions of the input uncertainty and takes full advantage of parallel computing. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework through numerical benchmarks.

2023.title: {PF}ES: Parallel Feasible Pareto Frontier Entropy Search for Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
2023.authors: J Qing, HB Moss, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
2023.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics, 2565-2588, 2023
2023.tldr: {PF}2ES introduces a novel information-theoretic acquisition function for multi-objective Bayesian optimization, supporting unknown constraints and batch queries. It addresses the challenge of efficiently and accurately estimating mutual information between candidate evaluations and the feasible Pareto frontier. By utilizing a variational lower bound, {PF}2ES provides a low-cost, accurate estimate, overcoming the limitations of crude approximations or expensive inference in prior methods. Benchmarking demonstrates {PF}2ES achieves competitive optimization performance across synthetic and real-world design problems.
2023.abstract: We present Parallel Feasible Pareto Frontier Entropy Search ({PF}2ES) — a novel information-theoretic acquisition function for multi-objective Bayesian optimization supporting unknown constraints and batch queries. Due to the complexity of characterizing the mutual information between candidate evaluations and (feasible) Pareto frontiers, existing approaches must either employ crude approximations that significantly hamper their performance or rely on expensive inference schemes that substantially increase the optimization's computational overhead. By instead using a variational lower bound, {PF}2ES provides a low-cost and accurate estimate of the mutual information. We benchmark {PF}2ES against other information-theoretic acquisition functions, demonstrating its competitive performance for optimization across synthetic and real-world design problems.

2023.title: Trieste: Efficiently exploring the depths of black-box functions with tensorflow
2023.authors: V Picheny, J Berkeley, HB Moss, H Stojic, U Granta, SW Ober, A Artemev, ...
2023.tldr: Trieste is an open-source Python package for scalable Bayesian Optimization (BO) and active learning, leveraging TensorFlow 2.x. It provides a modular framework for plug-and-play integration of TensorFlow-based probabilistic models (e.g., GPflow, Keras NNs) and custom acquisition functions. Trieste efficiently addresses BO's sequential nature by preventing expensive computational graph retracing. Key features include flexible `AskTellOptimizer`/`BayesianOptimizer` interfaces, diverse model support, and optimized acquisition functions utilizing automatic differentiation, enabling robust and extensible black-box function exploration.
2023.abstract: We present Trieste, an open-source Python package for Bayesian optimization and active learning benefiting from the scalability and efficiency of TensorFlow. Our library enables the plug-and-play of popular TensorFlow-based models within sequential decision-making loops, e.g. Gaussian processes from GPflow or GPflux, or neural networks from Keras. This modular mindset is central to the package and extends to our acquisition functions and the internal dynamics of the decision-making loop, both of which can be tailored and extended by researchers or engineers when tackling custom use cases. Trieste is a research-friendly and production-ready toolkit backed by a comprehensive test suite, extensive documentation, and available at https://github.com/secondmind-labs/trieste.

2023.title: Bayesian active learning for engineering design and optimization under uncertainty

2022.title: Finding knees in bayesian multi-objective optimization
2022.authors: A Heidari, J Qing, S Rojas Gonzalez, J Branke, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
2022.venue: International Conference on Parallel Problem Solving from Nature, 104-117, 2022
2022.tldr: This paper introduces novel acquisition functions within Bayesian Multi-Objective Optimization to efficiently identify "knee" solutions on the Pareto front. Knees represent desirable trade-off points, and this work addresses their detection based on two specific definitions. The proposed acquisition functions enable data-efficient discovery of these solutions, minimizing costly evaluations. This approach effectively scales to problems with many objectives, demonstrating promising results on various benchmarks.
2022.abstract: Multi-objective optimization requires many evaluations to identify a sufficiently dense approximation of the Pareto front. Especially for a higher number of objectives, extracting the Pareto front might not be easy nor cheap. On the other hand, the Decision-Maker is not always interested in the entire Pareto front, and might prefer a solution where there is a desirable trade-off between different objectives. An example of an attractive solution is the knee point of the Pareto front, although the current literature differs on the definition of a knee. In this work, we propose to detect knee solutions in a data-efficient manner (i.e., with a limited number of time-consuming evaluations), according to two definitions of knees. In particular, we propose several novel acquisition functions in the Bayesian Optimization framework for detecting these knees, which allows for scaling to many objectives. The suggested acquisition functions are evaluated on various benchmarks with promising results.

2022.title: Adaptive sampling with automatic stopping for feasible region identification in engineering design
2022.authors: J Qing, N Knudde, F Garbuglia, D Spina, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene
2022.tldr: This paper presents an adaptive sampling methodology for identifying feasible regions in engineering design. It utilizes Gaussian process metamodels to estimate multi-constraint feasible regions, employing an information-based adaptive sampling strategy for sequential refinement. A novel framework is introduced to automatically stop the sampling process by estimating the metamodel's prediction accuracy. The proposed approach demonstrates improved efficiency, accuracy, and robustness compared to state-of-the-art techniques.
2022.abstract: Engineering design is a complex process to find a suitable trade-off among different, and sometimes conflicting, design specifications. In reality, these requirements can be often considered as constraints of the design problem, that can be defined in terms of performance measures or geometrical characteristics of the device under study. In this paper, a new design space exploration methodology is presented for discovering feasible regions in the design space, where the term feasible region indicates the set of all design configurations satisfying all constraints of the design problem. The proposed method is based on Gaussian process metamodels to estimate the feasible region and leverages a information-based adaptive sampling technique to sequentially refine the prediction accuracy, which is applicable for multiple constraints problems. To efficiently stop the adaptive sampling process, a novel framework to estimate the metamodel’s prediction accuracy is proposed. The efficiency, accuracy and robustness of the proposed approach are compared with state-of-art techniques on suitable benchmark problems and practical engineering examples.

2022.title: A robust bayesian optimization framework for microwave circuit design under uncertainty
2022.authors: D De Witte, J Qing, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene, D Vande Ginste, D Spina
2022.tldr: This paper presents a novel, data-efficient Bayesian Optimization framework for robust microwave circuit design under inevitable parameter uncertainties. It achieves robustness by modifying the Expected Improvement (EI) criterion to explicitly account for design parameter variations like manufacturing tolerances. This approach efficiently identifies designs insensitive to uncertainties early in the design cycle, significantly improving robustness with fewer simulations compared to standard methods, as validated by application examples.
2022.abstract: In modern electronics, there are many inevitable uncertainties and variations of design parameters that have a profound effect on the performance of a device. These are, among others, induced by manufacturing tolerances, assembling inaccuracies, material diversities, machining errors, etc. This prompts wide interests in enhanced optimization algorithms that take the effect of these uncertainty sources into account and that are able to find robust designs, i.e., designs that are insensitive to the uncertainties early in the design cycle. In this work, a novel machine learning-based optimization framework that accounts for uncertainty of the design parameters is presented. This is achieved by using a modified version of the expected improvement criterion. Moreover, a data-efficient Bayesian Optimization framework is leveraged to limit the number of simulations required to find a robust design solution. Two suitable application examples validate that the robustness is significantly improved compared to standard design methods.

2022.title: Spectral representation of robustness measures for optimization under input uncertainty
2022.authors: J Qing, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
2022.tldr: This paper introduces a Spectral Representation of Robustness Measures (SRRM) to analytically infer mean-variance robustness under Gaussian Process (GP) models. Addressing the challenge of Bayesian variance inference, SRRM leverages GP's spectral representation to approximate robustness for normal and uniform input uncertainties. Two Fourier feature-based approximations are proposed and compared. Integrated into robust Bayesian Optimization acquisition functions, SRRM demonstrates competitive performance on numerical benchmarks and real-world applications.
2022.abstract: We study the inference of mean-variance robustness measures to quantify input uncertainty under the Gaussian Process (GP) framework. These measures are widely used in applications where the robustness of the solution is of interest, for example, in engineering design. While the variance is commonly used to characterize the robustness, Bayesian inference of the variance using GPs is known to be challenging. In this paper, we propose a Spectral Representation of Robustness Measures based on the GP’s spectral representation, i.e., an analytical approach to approximately infer both robustness measures for normal and uniform input uncertainty distributions. We present two approximations based on different Fourier features and compare their accuracy numerically. To demonstrate their utility and efficacy in robust Bayesian Optimization, we integrate the analytical robustness measures in three standard acquisition functions for various robust optimization formulations. We show their competitive performance on numerical benchmarks and real-life applications.

2021.title: Hovering efficiency optimization of the ducted propeller with weight penalty taken into account
2021.authors: Y Hu, J xiang Qing, ZH Liu, ZJ Conrad, JN Cao, XP Zhang
2021.tldr: This paper optimizes ducted propeller hovering efficiency, incorporating structural weight penalty. It reveals weight penalty dominates at low disk loading, while aerodynamic efficiency is key at high disk loading. Multi-objective optimization shows ducted propellers can surpass open propellers in overall efficiency, even at low disk loading. Optimal designs feature a large inner lip radius, small outer lip radius, and a short/no diffuser. This emphasizes the inner lip's primary aerodynamic contribution, achieving significant weight reduction with limited efficiency loss for compact, easily integrated systems.
2021.abstract: The ducted propeller is superior to the open propeller in hovering efficiency. However, the overall system efficiency of a ducted propeller is reduced due to its heavy structure. If the weight penalty is taken into account, will the ducted propeller still be superior to an open propeller? And in this scenario, how will a ducted propeller with better efficiency than an open propeller be designed? This paper investigates these questions by parametric analysis based on experiments and then parametric optimization that involves hovering efficiency and structural weight in objective functions. Both multi-disciplinary design optimization and multi-objective programming are performed by surrogate-based optimization. An in-house automatic structured mesh generation module is developed to deal with significant geometry variation in design space. Finally, the optimization results are validated by post-optimization experiments. The results of experiment and optimization indicate that the effects of weight penalty play a leading role at low disk loading and hence in this case, the one with lighter structure is superior. But at high disk loading, as thrust gets higher, the leading factor turns into aerodynamic hovering efficiency, therefore the one with higher aerodynamic hovering efficiency prevails. The multi-objective optimization produces an L-shaped Pareto front, and the optimum of multi-disciplinary optimization is quite close to the Pareto front knee point. The designs in this region encounter limited aerodynamic hovering efficiency loss but gain significant weight reduction. Therefore, we can obtain a ducted propeller superior to an open propeller in system efficiency with pretty low disk loading, although the weight penalty is considered. These designs feature a relatively large inner lip radius, a small outer lip radius, and a short or even no diffuser. This means that the inner lip radius contributes the most to the aerodynamic hovering efficiency, followed by the diffuser and outer lip. These designs have very low height to diameter ratio therefore they can be easily integrated into aircraft structure.

2021.title: Bayesian active learning for multi‐objective feasible region identification in microwave devices
2021.authors: F Garbuglia, J Qing, N Knudde, D Spina, I Couckuyt, D Deschrijver, ...
2021.tldr: This paper presents a novel Bayesian active learning framework for multi-objective feasible region identification in microwave device design. It leverages a stochastic model to efficiently and accurately pinpoint designs satisfying multiple specifications, significantly reducing the number of simulations required. The proposed automated procedure rapidly obtains suitable designs, validated through an application example, offering a more resource-efficient design optimization approach.
2021.abstract: In microwave device and circuit design, many simulations are often needed to find a set of designs that satisfy one or multiple specifications chosen by the designer upfront: the feasible region. A novel Bayesian active learning framework is presented to accurately identify the feasible region with a low number of simulations. The technique leverages on a stochastic model to obtain an efficient and automated procedure. A suitable application example validates the proposed technique and shows its effectiveness to rapidly obtain many suitable designs.

2020.title: Batch Bayesian active learning for feasible region identification by local penalization
2020.authors: J Qing, N Knudde, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene, K Shintani
2020.tldr: This paper proposes a batch Bayesian active learning technique for efficiently identifying feasible regions in engineering design, overcoming the high cost of constraint evaluations. Unlike sequential methods, it selects multiple samples per iteration, leveraging computational resources. The method assumes Lipschitz continuous constraint functions and extends existing batch active learning techniques to this specific task. Experiments demonstrate its superior performance in feasible region identification compared to these extended state-of-the-art batch methods.
2020.abstract: Identifying all designs satisfying a set of constraints is an important part of the engineering design process. With physics-based simulation codes, evaluating the constraints becomes considerable expensive. Active learning can provide an elegant approach to efficiently characterize the feasible region, i.e., the set of feasible designs. Although active learning strategies have been proposed for this task, most of them are dealing with adding just one sample per iteration as opposed to selecting multiple samples per iteration, also known as batch active learning. While this is efficient with respect to the amount of information gained per iteration, it neglects available computation resources. We propose a batch Bayesian active learning technique for feasible region identification by assuming that the constraint function is Lipschitz continuous. In addition, we extend current state-of-the-art batch methods to also handle feasible region identification. Experiments show better performance of the proposed method than the extended batch methods.

2020.title: Bayesian active learning for electromagnetic structure design
2020.authors: J Qing, N Knudde, I Couckuyt, D Spina, T Dhaene
2020.venue: 2020 14th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP), 1-5, 2020
2020.tldr: This paper presents a novel Bayesian active learning framework for electromagnetic structure design. It utilizes an entropy search-based strategy, powered by a Gaussian Process model, to efficiently identify design configurations that meet specific requirements. The core contribution is minimizing the number of time-consuming computer simulations or expensive design trials needed, thereby accelerating the design process. An application example validates its effectiveness.
2020.abstract: A novel design framework based on Bayesian active learning is presented in this contribution. The proposed approach allows one to identify a set of design configurations satisfying the chosen specification. In particular, the entropy search-based active learning strategy, which relies on a Gaussian Process model, is able to minimize the number of time-consuming computer simulations or expensive design trials necessary to reach this goal. A suitable application example validates the proposed method.

2019.title: Kriging Assisted Integrated Rotor-Duct Optimization for Ducted Fan in Hover
2019.authors: J Qing, Y Hu, Y Wang, Z Liu, X Fu, W Liu
2019.tldr: This paper presents a Kriging-assisted integrated rotor-duct optimization for ducted fans in hover, addressing limitations of separate optimizations. Using RANS with FFD/Bezier parameterizations, the objective was to maximize hovering efficiency under thrust constraints. Key finding: Integrated optimization achieves superior efficiency. It yields blades with longer tip chords, which injects more momentum into the duct's boundary layer, suppressing flow separation. This enables a larger diffuser expansion angle, resulting in a better overall hovering efficiency compared to un-integrated designs.
2019.abstract: The design of ducted fan was primarily based on parametric analysis and the existing optimization design studies mainly focus on either the rotor or the duct alone. However, the interactions between the rotor and duct remarkably affects the performance of the ducted fan. Therefore, it has been expected that an integrated optimization such the rotor-duct interactions are involved could result in a better design. In this paper, the integrated rotor-duct optimization was performed. Then it was compared with several different optimized configurations. The Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes solver incorporated with momentum source method was adopted to predict performance of ducted fan and it was validated by force measurement experiments. The duct shape was parameterized by the FFD method and the blade shape was modeled by Bezier splines. A surrogate based optimization framework using Kriging model was developed. The hovering efficiency was set as the objective function subjecting to the thrust constraint. The optima from different optimized configurations were analyzed with the help of crossover studies. The analysis revealed that the improvement of the ducted fan hovering efficiency is primarily restricted by the flow separations in the duct. When the shape of both the rotor and duct was involved into the design optimization, the blade with longer chord at blade tip was obtained. This helps injecting more momentum into the boundary layer of the duct and the flow separation can be suppressed. Therefore, the integrated rotor-duct optimization produces the duct with larger diffuser expansion angle and better hovering efficiency.
